sentences.en: On Saturday, my friend and I went to the store to buy some things.
I saw a book and said, "I want to buy this book."
The clerk smiled and said, "For books you should say 'yì běn,' not 'yí gè.'"
This time, I bought a cup of coffee and a piece of cake.
My friend said, "Now you've got it!"
I still wanted to buy a piece of clothing, but I was running low on money.

quiz.q: What mistake does the narrator make with the book?
a: Says 一个 instead of 一本
Says 一杯 instead of 一本

quiz.q: What does the narrator buy correctly the second time?
Why doesn't the narrator buy the clothing?

grammar.p: measure word + noun（量词 + 名词）
grammar.e: A number needs a specific measure word before the noun — not just 个 for everything: 一本书 (a book), 一杯咖啡 (a cup of coffee), 一块蛋糕 (a piece of cake), 一件衣服 (a piece of clothing).
grammar.x: 我要买一本书，不是一个书。 — I want to buy a book, not "yí gè shū."

grammar.p: 一 changes tone before a measure word
grammar.e: 一 is yì before a 1st/2nd/3rd-tone measure word (like 本, 杯) and yí before a 4th-tone one (like 个, 件, 块).
grammar.x: 一杯咖啡 (yì bēi)、一个人 (yí gè).

grammar.p: 会 + 了（now you can do it）
grammar.e: 会 means 'know how to'; adding 了 shows a change — you couldn't before, but now you can.
grammar.x: 你现在会了！ — Now you've got it!
